subject: Decision: LedgerWorks onboarding - per-tenant export filter (scope & trade-offs)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@ledgerworks.com>
Cc: procurement@ledgerworks.com
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: LedgerWorks onboarding - per-tenant export filter: decision needed

Marissa / Ben / Aditya / Sarah —

Quick context: LedgerWorks wants to onboard next quarter and procurement has asked us to commit to a per-tenant export filtering capability (ability to configure export rules that only surface a subset of tenant data for downstream S3 exports). They framed it as a gating security/control requirement for their audit team.

Attached is the spreadsheet LedgerWorks sent with the minimal acceptance criteria (LedgerWorks_MVP_requirements.xlsx). From a commercial standpoint we have an executed term sheet pending a narrow SOW in DocuSign (link below in metadata). Customer expectation: go-live window mid-July.

Ask: we need an explicit product/eng decision on whether we can deliver a scoped MVP (filtering by tenant metadata + allowlist for export destinations) by 2027-07-15, or whether we should propose a phased approach where we ship an export whitelist first and follow with server-side filtering in a later sprint.

Key trade-offs I think we should consider:
- Time-to-close: committing to the full filter likely accelerates procurement but increases engineering scope.
- Risk: server-side filtering touches runtime routing and export pipeline; potential perf/regression risk.
- Commercial: LedgerWorks is asking for a two-week pilot and an SLA uplift if we take on the full work now.

Can you weigh in with prefered option, suggested acceptance criteria for an MVP, and realistic engineering ETA? If product/eng sign off, I'll confirm with the customer and update the SOW.

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@ledgerworks.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: LedgerWorks onboarding - per-tenant export filter: decision needed

Jonas — thanks for the clear summary and the attachment. High level product take: we can do a pragmatic phased approach that minimizes runtime changes and still addresses LedgerWorks' auditor asks. Proposal:

Phase 1 (MVP, target 2027-07-15):
- Admin UI / API to configure export allowlists (per-tenant) for destination buckets
- Export orchestration respects allowlist (i.e., only exports to configured destinations for that tenant)
- Audit log entries for export events (tenant id, destination, timestamp)

Phase 2 (post-go-live, targeted 4-week sprint):
- Server-side filtering during export generation (exclude records based on tenant filters before entering export pipeline)
- Unit + integration QA focused on perf impact

Why phased: building server-side filtering requires changes to KV cache handling and the export pipeline; that increases test surface and likely needs an extra 2–3 weeks of engineering plus regression window. Phase 1 buys time and addresses the core compliance ask (control where exports land).

If Sales pushes for Phase 2 in the initial SOW we need a 4–6 week slippage on the target.

Marissa Cole
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: LedgerWorks onboarding - per-tenant export filter: decision needed

Short technical take and ETA from Eng:

We can commit to Phase 1 as defined by Marissa without touching the hot path code that serves inference requests. Implementation notes:
- Build an export allowlist service (stateless) that the orchestration layer will query before emitting export jobs. This avoids touching KV/serving runtime.
- Add audit events to the export worker (small change, low risk).
- Estimated effort: 2.5 engineer-weeks (one backend engineer + one infra/qa) to ship, 1 week for integration/regress. Realistic target date for Phase 1: 2027-07-14 if prioritized immediately.

For Phase 2 (server-side filtering before export generation) — non-trivial: entails injecting a filtering step in the export generation flow and adding cache invalidation paths. I would plan 4 engineer-weeks plus a 2-week regression window. That would push ship to late August if done up-front.

Risks / notes:
- If we agree to an SLA uplift we should negotiate a commercial buffer for performance incidents related to export pipeline changes.
- We will want a pilot tenant (LedgerWorks can provide a staging bucket) to validate regressions before go-live.

Ben Carter
Head of Engineering, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
